narrative.text: The text of World Health Assembly resolution WHA64.5 (May 2011), which welcomes the outcome of the open-ended working group, acknowledges industry's role in innovation and technology transfer, adopts the PIP Framework and asks the Director-General to report on its implementation.

Sets out the principles of the PIP Framework, in which WHO Member States recall earlier resolutions, note the persistent risk of a catastrophic influenza pandemic, especially for developing countries, and commit to sharing H5N1 and other potentially pandemic viruses on an equal footing with benefit-sharing. The principles reaffirm obligations under the International Health Regulations (2005), address intellectual property, and call for technology transfer and financing to make vaccines more affordable for developing countries. The objective is to strengthen the WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System for fair, transparent and equitable virus sharing and access to vaccines and other benefits.
Defines the scope of the Framework: sharing of H5N1 and other potentially pandemic influenza viruses and benefit-sharing, excluding seasonal influenza and non-influenza pathogens.
Introduces the section on definitions and terminology used in the Framework.

Defines "PIP biological materials" as human clinical specimens, wild-type virus isolates of H5N1 and other potentially pandemic influenza viruses, modified viruses developed by WHO GISRS laboratories, and related RNA and cDNA.

Defines further technical terms used in the Framework, such as genetic sequences, reference reagents, candidate vaccine viruses and wild-type viruses, with an operational exception noted in a footnote.

Defines the institutions and entities referred to in the Framework, including essential regulatory laboratories, manufacturers of influenza diagnostics, vaccines and medicines, national influenza centres and WHO collaborating centres. It explains that WHO GISRS comprises these laboratory types.
Defines other terms used in the Framework, such as Advisory Group, affected countries, least developed countries and originating laboratory, and introduces the section on the virus-sharing system.
A heading fragment for the section on the system for sharing H5N1 and other potentially pandemic influenza viruses.

Sets out general provisions for virus sharing: Member States should rapidly and systematically provide PIP biological materials from all cases to a WHO collaborating centre or H5 reference laboratory of their choice. It also covers consent for onward transfer and sharing with other laboratories, provided WHO laboratories receive materials first.

Calls for rapid sharing of genetic sequence data on H5N1 and other potentially pandemic viruses with the originating laboratory and among GISRS laboratories, and for the Advisory Group to advise on handling sequence data given trends towards public databases.

Requires the Director-General to set up a transparent electronic traceability mechanism to track PIP biological materials in real time and give feedback to originating laboratories and countries. It allows modifications in a pandemic emergency limited to the relevant strains, to be reported to Member States.
States that Standard Material Transfer Agreement 1 governs transfers within GISRS and that SMTA 2 will be used for transfers to entities outside the system.
The opening line of the general considerations on the PIP benefit-sharing system, on Member States working with the WHO Secretariat.

Calls on stakeholders, including manufacturers and researchers, to support the PIP benefit-sharing system and sets out its aims, such as pandemic surveillance, risk assessment and early warning for all countries. It also aims to provide benefits to Member States based on public health risk and need, especially developing countries.

States that WHO will coordinate pandemic influenza preparedness and response under the International Health Regulations (2005) and the Framework, with attention to fair, equitable and transparent allocation of scarce medical resources such as vaccines and antivirals.

Requires GISRS laboratories to share summaries of their analyses of PIP materials with WHO and originating countries to support risk response, and WHO to share information on vaccines and other responses. It also encourages support for research and surveillance capacity, including staff training.

Requires WHO collaborating centres and other designated laboratories to supply candidate vaccine viruses on request to manufacturers on a non-preferential basis and to laboratories, with recipients following WHO biosafety guidance.

Commits WHO laboratories to keep providing free non-commercial diagnostic reagents and tests to national influenza centres, and urges diagnostic manufacturers receiving PIP materials to offer reagents on preferential terms.
Commits essential regulatory laboratories to supply reference reagents for vaccine potency and training in quality control for pandemic vaccines to national regulators and manufacturers.

Encourages Member States with advanced influenza laboratory and surveillance capacity to help developing countries build national capacity for early virus detection, risk assessment, research and qualification of laboratories within GISRS.

Calls on Member States with advanced regulatory capacity to help developing countries strengthen regulatory authorities so they can rapidly approve safe and effective influenza diagnostics, vaccines and medicines, including those derived from PIP materials.

Commits the Director-General to work with partners and manufacturers to maintain and expand a WHO stockpile of antivirals to contain H5N1 and other potentially pandemic outbreaks, seeking expert advice on its size, composition and use.

Commits WHO to build and maintain a stockpile of vaccines against H5N1 and other potentially pandemic viruses, initially 150 million doses, with indicative allocations to affected and developing countries on expert advice. It covers related supplies and the development and testing of operational plans for allocation.

Calls on Member States to encourage vaccine manufacturers to set aside part of each H5N1 production run for stockpiling or use by developing countries, and to collaborate so these countries can obtain sufficient vaccine according to public health risk.

Calls for manufacturers to reserve part of pandemic vaccine production for developing countries and for an expert group to develop international mechanisms for distributing pandemic vaccine according to risk and need. It also addresses tiered pricing, taking account of the vulnerability of least developed countries.

Commits WHO to continue implementing the Global Pandemic Influenza Action Plan to increase vaccine supply, including new production capacity and technology transfer to developing countries. It urges manufacturers to transfer technology and know-how and encourages countries to adopt seasonal influenza vaccination to sustain production.

Sets out sustainable financing for the PIP benefit-sharing system, including an annual partnership contribution from manufacturers using GISRS, to be split between preparedness and response activities. It explains how contributions are distributed among companies and how WHO's operating costs are covered.
A section heading: governance and review.

States that the World Health Assembly will oversee the Framework, advised by the Director-General, and sets out an oversight mechanism comprising the Assembly, the Director-General and an independent Advisory Group of international experts, with their respective roles.

Explains that the Advisory Group advises the Director-General with evidence-based reports and recommendations but has no administrative or public role. It describes its establishment, membership drawn from the six WHO regions and affected countries, functions and reporting to the Sixty-fifth World Health Assembly.

Requires the terms of reference of GISRS laboratories to follow the guiding principles in Annex 4 and sets out how compliance is monitored. It allows the Director-General to suspend or revoke a laboratory's WHO designation for serious breaches.

Requires the Director-General to report every two years on laboratory and surveillance capacity, global vaccine production capacity, industry agreements and finances, with a review of the Framework and annexes by 2016.

The Framework's annexes, beginning with the full text of Standard Material Transfer Agreement 1 for transfers within GISRS, covering parties, purpose, sharing obligations, acknowledgement of contributors and a bar on seeking intellectual property rights over the materials. Further annexes set out SMTA 2 and the terms of reference of the Advisory Group, including membership terms, regional representation and working methods. It closes by introducing Annex 4 on guiding principles for the terms of reference of GISRS laboratories.

Sets out guiding principles for the terms of reference of GISRS laboratories working on potentially pandemic viruses, covering prompt sharing of materials and analyses, involvement of originating laboratories, and transfer of materials under SMTA 1. It then introduces Annex 5 on WHO collaborating centres.

Annex 5 sets out the terms of reference for work on PIP biological materials by the different types of GISRS laboratories, beginning with background on GISRS as a global alert mechanism and the core terms of reference for WHO collaborating centres. It goes on to cover the roles of H5 reference laboratories, national influenza centres and essential regulatory laboratories. Provisions include sharing analyses, supplying candidate vaccine viruses and reagents, and involving scientists from originating countries, especially developing countries, in research and publication. The annex ends with commitments to support global health emergency preparedness and the publication's ISBN and WHO address.

The front matter of the French edition of WHO's Pandemic Influenza Preparedness (PIP) Framework for the sharing of influenza viruses and access to vaccines and other benefits, reprinted in 2013, with cataloguing data, ISBN, copyright and disclaimers, a table of contents and the opening of resolution WHA64.5.
